declared_purpose: Autonomous iterative development through requirements interviews, planning, one-task build iterations and generic refinement, with a dashboard and archived run history (SKILL.md:5-10,69-104,136-182). The entry recommends limiting credentials and private-data access to task requirements (SKILL.md:511-515).

data_operations.operation: Gather requirements and persist task instructions
data_operations.data_scope: Intended users, needs, success criteria, functional requirements, edge cases and dependencies; generic task prompts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking assistant and human; project specs/*.md; generated /tmp/ralph-prompt-<task>.md.
data_operations.condition: Interview guidance requires human approval before planning; generic-loop guidance creates a prompt file.

data_operations.operation: Read project context, delegate analysis and save development progress
data_operations.data_scope: Specifications, implementation plan, source code, search findings, validation results and operational learnings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Claude and instructed Sonnet/Opus subagents; project source, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, AGENTS.md and occasionally specifications.
data_operations.condition: When these templates are used. Context study and delegation are explicit instructions; planning prohibits implementation, while building selects one important task.

data_operations.operation: Inspect the local application through a browser
data_operations.data_scope: Rendered application layout, styling and displayed data.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browser tool and its invoking agent.
data_operations.condition: Explicitly required for visual work. Further browser handling is unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Read prompt, resume state and completion marker
data_operations.data_scope: Prompt-file contents or inline prompt; existing state JSON; done-file contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Runner process memory.
data_operations.condition: Existing prompt paths are read; otherwise the argument is treated as text. Existing valid state is resumed unless --fresh applies.

data_operations.operation: Pass each iteration to a Claude subprocess and collect its return
data_operations.data_scope: Task prompt, iteration/max counters, completion signal and done-file path; returned response, usage, cost and stderr.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local claude child process; returned data in runner memory. Downstream service handling is unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Each iteration invokes claude with permission bypass and JSON output from ~/clawd. Model override is optional. The response is not added to normal iteration-history entries.

data_operations.operation: Feed a selected prompt to the shell-loop Claude process
data_operations.data_scope: PROMPT_plan.md or PROMPT_build.md; CLI output configured as verbose.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Claude process through stdin; terminal output.
data_operations.condition: Each shell iteration, in the operator's project directory, with permission bypass and the opus model.

data_operations.operation: Stage, commit and publish Git changes
data_operations.data_scope: All nonignored working-tree changes selected by git add -A; commits, tags and branch objects needed by a push.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Git index/object database; configured push remote, explicitly origin/current branch in the shell wrapper.
data_operations.condition: The building template explicitly commands add, commit and push after tests pass. The shell separately attempts a push after every iteration in either phase when it detects Git.

data_operations.operation: Describe an optional direct API disclosure
data_operations.source: Documented replacement for an unavailable Claude CLI
data_operations.data_scope: Messages supplied by the operator, model settings and an API-key authentication header using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages.
data_operations.condition: Only if the operator implements this alternative. The example leaves messages unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Persist active run state
data_operations.data_scope: Run name, session identifier, state-file path, timestamps, iteration/status fields, and history containing timing/token counters or errors.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Explicit --state location or generated /tmp/ralph-*.json.
data_operations.condition: Saved at startup and during progress, failures and termination. This supports resume and dashboard monitoring.

data_operations.operation: Print task and process details
data_operations.data_scope: First 60 characters of promptArg, name, session identifier, state path and check command; up to 500 response characters, 300 raw-output characters and 200 stderr characters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Runner stdout/stderr; any external console capture is unknown.
data_operations.condition: Startup details print regardless of --quiet; response/raw-output/stderr excerpts are conditional on nonquiet execution.

data_operations.operation: Execute an optional control command and retain its result
data_operations.data_scope: Command output or error text; STOP decision and failure reason.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Runner memory and console; full selected reason text in state JSON and subsequently its archive.
data_operations.condition: Only when configured. STOP output or command failure halts the loop; other output is logged in nonquiet mode. The command's own data operations are unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Archive, overwrite and delete run-control files
data_operations.data_scope: State JSON and done-marker contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/clawd/logs/ralph-archive/ receives copies; active state and done files are then deleted.
data_operations.condition: Normal completion and loop termination invoke archiving. --fresh deletes existing selected state/done files; startup clears the done file. Archive failures can leave files behind. This does not delete project work or generated prompt files.

data_operations.operation: Read loop files and infer operational status
data_operations.data_scope: Matching /tmp/ralph-*.json, associated done markers, every archive JSON, file metadata and histories; derived status, success, token/cost/duration totals.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Dashboard process memory.
data_operations.condition: On dashboard reader calls. Completion uses marker contents; success uses done, absence of recorded errors and positive token counts. These are operational inferences.

data_operations.operation: Return dashboard records to HTTP clients
data_operations.source: Mounted RalphReader routes and served index page
data_operations.data_scope: Loop names/identifiers, local file paths, session identifiers, status/timestamps, histories and aggregates. Default listing includes 50 archives; the archived endpoint accepts a requested limit.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requesting HTTP client/browser; remote clients can receive responses if they can reach the listener.
data_operations.condition: The served page fetches listings initially and every three seconds, and history when selected. Mounted routes show no authentication; CORS permits all origins and listen has no explicit loopback host.

data_operations.operation: Log HTTP requests and report errors
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, method, complete request URL including query string; exception details.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Dashboard stdout/stderr; route error.message also returns to the originating HTTP client.
data_operations.condition: Each request and applicable error path. Log capture and retention are unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Find and stop loop processes
data_operations.data_scope: Loop/session identifiers, identifier suffix and matching process IDs; completion marker.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process-search/termination commands; active done file; requesting client receives a result message.
data_operations.condition: POST /api/loops/:id/kill for a located active loop. It writes a stop marker and retains state; this is termination rather than data deletion.

data_operations.operation: Inspect gateway sessions and infer loop patterns or labels
data_operations.data_scope: Gateway session records; session age/key/label; transcript inventory and metadata; task-derived labels truncated to 50 characters; repetition severity.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Component memory and its caller. Session keys are sent to the gateway on chat.abort.
data_operations.condition: Only if separately called: the supplied server/router uses RalphReader. getLoopAnalysis filters subagents; getAllSessions includes all available sessions/transcripts. Gateway transport is unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Read transcripts and derive usage/cost metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Local JSONL messages, thinking blocks, labels, session keys, timestamps and usage/cost fields; malformed raw lines.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Helper/caller memory; class-reader parse warnings print the malformed line to the caller's console.
data_operations.condition: Only if invoked. Class transcripts are returned to their caller; getLoopAnalysis returns counts and usage metadata. No transcript HTTP route is implemented by the supplied router.

data_operations.operation: Install external software
data_operations.source: Setup instructions and dashboard startup script
data_operations.data_scope: Package/dependency installation requests and downloaded artifacts; further installer behavior is unresolved.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured npm registry; dashboard lock entries resolve registry.npmjs.org. Packages are installed locally.
data_operations.condition: Manual setup, or dashboard/start.sh when node_modules is absent. Registry and funding URLs alone do not establish runtime telemetry.

data_operations.operation: Describe optional local test and backup persistence
data_operations.data_scope: Test counter and prompt; copies or compressed snapshots of src/.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp test files; project backups/iteration-* or snapshots/pre-iteration-*.tar.gz.
data_operations.condition: Only when the optional test is run or the operator modifies the loop to use documented backups.

potential_excess.data_scope: Loop records, histories, names, identifiers and local paths.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Any HTTP client able to reach the dashboard port; cross-origin browser clients are permitted.
potential_excess.condition: Dashboard running with the supplied listener and middleware; actual network reachability is unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Setup presents a localhost monitoring interface. Broader listener/origin access is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Let the intended operator view progress and history.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Bind to loopback for local use and restrict origins; require authenticated access if remote monitoring is intentionally enabled.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the local dashboard and explicitly authorized remote access.

potential_excess.data_scope: sessionId, stateFile/archiveFile paths and full iteration histories embedded in listing records.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Clients of loop-listing endpoints, including the repeatedly polling dashboard.
potential_excess.condition: Normal listing requests; these fields accompany required summary data.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Cards display summary fields, while a separate history endpoint serves selected history. This is extra data within a required response.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: List names, opaque loop IDs, status, timestamps and aggregate progress.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return allowlisted summary records; omit filesystem paths and session IDs, and fetch history only when selected.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep server-side identifiers needed for stopping loops and preserve authorized detail/history access.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated, nonignored working-tree files or edits.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local Git commits and the configured push remote.
potential_excess.condition: Such changes coexist with the selected build task when git add -A runs.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The template explicitly requires broad staging, but the declared iteration outcome is one selected task. Narrowing requires changing that instruction.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Commit and publish the selected task and its required supporting changes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Stage reviewed task-specific paths rather than every working-tree change.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Include required specifications, plan updates, tests, generated files and dependencies; retain the required commit/push outcome.

potential_excess.data_scope: Current branch updates and unpublished Git objects, potentially predating the planning task.
potential_excess.condition: Shell planning iterations when Git is detected.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Planning explicitly requires a local prioritized plan. The wrapper additionally publishes after every phase.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Skip automatic pushes in planning mode unless plan publication is requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain explicitly requested publication and the build workflow's required pushes.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second Git push invocation and associated remote negotiation.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The same origin/current branch already updated by the build agent.
potential_excess.condition: The template-side push succeeded to that same destination and no subsequent changes require publication.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Both template and wrapper command a push. This can be a redundant action; duplicate content transfer is not established.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Publish each intended branch update successfully.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Assign publication to one component or skip the wrapper push when already synchronized.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve retries and remote-branch creation when the first publication failed or targeted a different destination.

potential_excess.data_scope: Inline prompt excerpts, task response/raw-output excerpts, stderr and full check-command text.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Node runner stdout/stderr and any configured console capture.
potential_excess.condition: Startup details always print; response-related excerpts print in nonquiet mode.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Autonomous completion uses file progress and a done marker. Content-bearing console excerpts are diagnostic implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report progress, completion and actionable failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Default to counters/status and redacted error summaries; make task-content logging opt-in and apply quiet mode to startup details.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Allow explicitly requested debugging without losing completion signaling or useful failure status.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete selected control-command stdout, stderr or error text stored as a stop/failure reason.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Active state JSON and its durable archive copy.
potential_excess.condition: --check-cmd returns STOP or fails; output contains more than the control decision requires.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The command provides stop control. Persisting unbounded output is additional data within that required control action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record whether control requested a stop or failed.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Store a reason code, exit status and bounded redacted explanation instead of complete output.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve STOP detection and operator-requested diagnostic detail.

potential_excess.data_scope: Archived done-marker contents, including empty or completion-marker files.
potential_excess.condition: A done file exists during archiving.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The live marker controls completion; archived status is already represented by JSON and filename, and the archive reader consumes JSON files.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the marker until live completion is detected and retain the run's final status.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the redundant marker archive copy; retain any needed stop provenance as minimal structured metadata.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove the live completion mechanism or explicitly required audit provenance.

potential_excess.data_scope: Older run names, identifiers, paths, per-iteration records and optional command-error reasons.
potential_excess.condition: Runs accumulate; the supplied archive implementation has no expiry. Required retention duration is unresolved.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Archival is explicitly declared, but indefinite retention of every detailed run is not specified; the default listing displays 50 archives.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide required recent history and useful aggregate statistics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Introduce configurable retention and aggregate older records before deleting unnecessary detail.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Set retention requirements first; preserve active resume state, explicitly requested long-term history and aggregate statistics.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full parsed message and thinking bodies retained solely to calculate transcript counts.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: TranscriptReader and LoopDetector process memory; only summary metadata subsequently returns from getLoopAnalysis.
potential_excess.condition: The otherwise unwired getLoopAnalysis component is separately invoked.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: That caller needs message count, token total and thinking-block count. Reading relevant records is necessary; retaining their full bodies is additional processing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a summary reader that accumulates counts and usage without retaining message/thinking bodies.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve parsing/count semantics and keep full transcript access separate for callers that actually require it.

potential_excess.condition: The packaged class reader is invoked and JSON parsing fails; this is not a mounted dashboard transcript route.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Parsing diagnostics need an error location, rather than the complete potentially content-bearing record.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify malformed records and continue processing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log session identifier, line number and error category without raw content.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain useful diagnostics and optional explicitly enabled redacted debugging.

potential_excess.data_scope: User-supplied query strings and loop identifiers embedded in complete request URLs.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Dashboard stdout and any console log collector.
potential_excess.condition: Requests contain details beyond what routing diagnostics require.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Request logging is an implementation choice; full URLs are unnecessary for basic service monitoring.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Observe request timing, route and outcome.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log route templates and status while omitting query values and unnecessary identifiers.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain limited correlation identifiers when operationally required; configure capture retention separately.

unknowns: Claude CLI implementation and configuration are absent. Actual model endpoints, context-file reads, credential use, telemetry, remote payloads and provider retention cannot be determined. The Node spawn supplies no explicit environment filter.

Clawdbot gateway implementation, transport, authentication, returned session fields and abort-side persistence are absent. Whether the otherwise unwired LoopDetector is integrated elsewhere is unknown.
Actual prompts, specifications, repository contents, unrelated edits, Git remotes, unpublished history and credential environment are unavailable; actual sensitive disclosures cannot be established.
Dashboard network reachability, firewall/proxy protections, browser restrictions and console capture destinations/retention are unknown. Public-internet exposure is not established.
Required archive retention and operating-system cleanup of /tmp are unspecified. Runner cleanup targets state/done files; generated task prompt lifetime remains unresolved.
npm, installed dependencies, Claude Code and optional alternative agents are external implementations. Their installation/runtime data handling cannot be audited from manifests and instructions.

The direct-API example leaves messages undefined. Arbitrary check commands, validation commands and task-specific applications can perform additional operations that the supplied source does not resolve.
